Panic is evil's weapon.

Commenting on the @claudeai FUD ↓

What happened:

• On 25 July 2026, a Reddit post demonstrated that a site-restricted Google search returned other users' shared Claude conversations.

• A follow-up thread the next morning showed the same technique working against published artifacts.

• The core claim is accurate: pages that users had shared or published were discoverable by people who had never been given the link.

BUT what people are amplifying on X materially overstates the scope.

This post from @om_patel5 asserts that essentially ALL published artifacts are indexed, enumerates categories of highly sensitive content (payroll data, cap tables, clinical trial records, tax documents), and states that third-party sites have begun aggregating scraped artifacts into browsable collections.

Classic fake news.

The first assertion is contradicted by how indexing works; the second is a list of hypothetical content types rather than a catalogue of verified findings.

The "leaked" were pages users explicitly set to public URLs, and that public artifacts are, definitionally, public.

Yeah, Claude's two-option UI offering "only me" or "anyone with the link" does not communicate "and search engines may list this," – but that's a different thing.

Thank you, FUD cancelled.
See ya later.

They will eliminate tasks for us around tax planning, portfolio rebalancing, and bill pay.

Welcome to the world of Agentic Finance (AiFi). This is what Coinbase is building.

The biggest barrier to people building something with zero dev experience when vibe coding (me) is that there’s still a large knowledge gap - if you don’t understand what’s happening then how can you build something with taste?

The solution is having the AI teach you whilst you build, for it to teach you what has been done? Why? How? What’s next? What could break? How could it be better? Whilst maintaining context on what has changed since last time? Why did it change? What does that mean for everything else?
